defendant: Treves, Inc., 615 Corporate Place, Fostoria, OH 44830. The complaint pleads at paragraph 2 that Treves 'has represented itself to JobsOhio as a Delaware corporation, but the Delaware Secretary of State records show no company by such name. (See Exhibit 1).' The court's 2024-11-14 agreed entry later found 'that Treves, Inc. has changed its name to Kotobukiya Treves Ohio, Inc., who shall be the party Defendant to these proceedings for all purposes.'
agreement: Grant Agreement. Complaint paragraph 4: 'On or about April 18, 2018, JobsOhio entered into a Grant Agreement with Defendant as the Grantee, a copy of which is attached hereto as Exhibit 2. Pursuant to the terms of the Grant Agreement, JobsOhio agreed to provide Defendant $200,000.00 in grant funds, on a reimbursement basis, conditioned on Defendant complying with all terms of the Grant Agreement, including achieving all metrics set forth in the Grant Agreement at its project site located at 615 Corporate Place, Fostoria, OH 44830.' The document attached as Exhibit 2 is headed 'JOBSOHIO GRANT AGREEMENT'.
agreement_date: The complaint says 'On or about April 18, 2018.' The agreement attached as Exhibit 2 states on its face 'Effective Date: October 30, 2017.' The 2023-07-20 demand letter (Exhibit 3) refers to 'the JobsOhio Grant Agreement in the amount of $200,000, dated April 18, 2018, as amended if applicable.' The complaint does not explain the two dates.
program: The complaint text names no JobsOhio program. The face of the attached agreement carries 'Program No.: SFPN_2017_441082-ED'. That is a contract number printed on the agreement, not a program name, and the complaint never says which of JobsOhio's published programs it belongs to.
amount_sought: $200,000.00, plus interest including prejudgment interest, reasonable attorney fees, costs and expenses. This is the full amount disbursed, not the $50,000 the 2023-07-20 demand letter asked for. Complaint paragraph 10 explains the step up: 'Defendant's failure to pay and return grant funds in the amount demanded by JobsOhio within 30 days as required under Section 9(b)(ii) of the Grant Agreement constitutes a further breach by Defendant, and JobsOhio therefore seeks damages in the entire amount of the grant funds provided to Defendant, being $200,000.00'.
job_commitments: Create 91 new jobs at the Project Site with a payroll of at least $3,400,000.00, and make fixed asset investments at the Project Site of $11,350,000.00 (the 'Metric Commitments'). Metric Evaluation Date December 31, 2020; Metric Expiration Date December 31, 2022. The face of the attached agreement repeats these: Total Fixed Asset Investment $11,350,000; No. of Jobs to be Created 91; Total Payroll to be Created $3,400,000.
shortfall: Complaint paragraph 8: 'pursuant to Defendant's 2022 Annual Report, Defendant only created 75 new jobs at the Project Site, instead of the required 91 new jobs.' The demand letter puts it the same way. Neither filing states what payroll or fixed asset investment was achieved.
repayment_quote: 5. Metrics and Maintenance of Operations. Grantor has approved an award of financial assistance to Grantee to induce Grantee to undertake and complete the Project with the goal of attracting and retaining business opportunities for the State of Ohio that create and/or retain a significant number of jobs for Ohioans. Accordingly, achieving Grantee's Metric Commitment obligations at the Project site during the Term are essential terms of this Agreement. *** (a) Metric Commitment. Grantee must attain all Metric Commitments set forth on the first page of this Agreement no later than the Metric Evaluation Date. Once Metric Commitments have been met, Grantee shall maintain such Metric Commitments through the Metric Expiration Date. *** (c) Remedy. If Grantee fails to satisfy its obligations under Section 5(a), Section 6(b), or to maintain substantial operations at the Project site during the Term, Grantee is in default of this Agreement and Grantor may seek the remedies provided to Grantor under section 9 of this Agreement. *** (Emphasis added). || (b) Annual Reports. Grantee shall submit to Grantor an annual report in the format required by Grantor (the 'Annual Report'). Each Annual Report shall provide information for the applicable reporting period detailing the progress of the Project, and Metric Commitments to date. Annual Reports shall be submitted by Grantee for each calendar year (or part of a year) during the Term of this Agreement, and each Annual Report shall be received by Grantor no later than March 1 following the calendar year covered by such Annual Report. Failure by Grantee to submit any Annual Report shall be a default for which Grantor may terminate this Agreement as set forth in Section 9. (Emphasis added). || (a) Breach. Grantee shall be deemed to be in 'Breach' of this Agreement if: *** (ii) Grantee fails to comply with the Metric Commitment requirements set forth in Section 5 hereof; (iii) Grantee fails to timely comply with its reporting obligations under Section 6 hereof; (iv) Grantee fails to maintain substantial operations at the Project Address during the Term. *** (b) Effect of Breach; Remedies. In the event of a Breach by Grantor, Grantee may pursue any legal or equitable remedies it may have under this Agreement or applicable law. In the event of a Breach by Grantee, Grantor may terminate this Agreement and may in addition exercise one or more of the following remedies: *** (ii) Demand Repayment of Grant Funds. Grantor may demand repayment of all or a portion of Grant Funds disbursed. Grantee shall repay such Grant Funds within thirty (30) days after written demand by Grantor. (Emphasis added). (iii) Other Legal Remedies. Pursue any other legal or equitable remedies Grantor may have under this Agreement or applicable law.
remedy_named: 'Demand Repayment of Grant Funds', Section 9(b)(ii). Not styled a clawback and not styled liquidated damages. The matching heading in Section 5(c) is 'Remedy'. Section 9(e) is cited for fees: Defendant is liable for JobsOhio's 'expenses, including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees, in connection with the enforcement of this Agreement.'
agreement_is_exhibit: Yes. The full signed Grant Agreement is attached as Exhibit 2, pages 8 through 15 of the 16-page filing, DocuSigned. Exhibit 1 is the Delaware Secretary of State search result; Exhibit 3 is the 2023-07-20 demand letter from Don Grubbs, JobsOhio General Counsel. This is one of the cases where the agreement itself reached the public record.
outcome: Settled, then dismissed with prejudice by JobsOhio. JobsOhio moved for default judgment on 2024-10-02; defense counsel appeared 2024-10-14 and filed a memo contra. On 2024-11-14 Judge Andria C. Noble signed an 'Agreed Entry to Stay Proceedings Pending Completion of Settlement Obligations': 'Upon motion of the parties, and for good cause shown, this case is hereby stayed pending completion of the settlement agreement entered into between the parties. Upon such completion, Plaintiff shall dismiss this case with prejudice. Should there be any breach of the settlement agreement, then Plaintiff shall notify the Court by filing written notice of the same, in which event the stay shall be automatically lifted, and these proceedings may continue.' The default motion was ruled moot the same day. On 2025-05-01 JobsOhio filed a 'Notice of Dismissal with Prejudice': 'Now come the Plaintiff JobsOhio and hereby dismisses this action with prejudice.' The case terminated that day.
amount_recovered: No filing states any figure. No judgment was entered and no satisfaction of judgment was filed. The settlement agreement is not in the record; only the agreed stay entry referring to it. Its terms and any sum paid are not public.

notes: Three things worth carrying forward. First, JobsOhio demanded $50,000 on 2023-07-20, a reduced figure that 'takes into account the number of jobs and payroll Grantee created, the total fixed assets invested in the Project, as well as the Market Conditions and Other Factors provided by Grantee to JobsOhio,' then sued for the full $200,000 when the 30 days ran out. The agreement lets it do that: Section 9(b)(ii) says 'all or a portion.' Second, the agreement is attached in full here, so the actual contract text, not just the complaint's excerpts, is on the public record in this case. Third, the complaint opens by saying the Delaware Secretary of State has no record of a company called Treves, Inc.; the defendant turned out to be Kotobukiya Treves Ohio, Inc. The company retained counsel, fought, and settled on undisclosed terms. Jobs shortfall was 75 of 91, about 82 percent.
